term: Derivation of the conjugate gradient method
definition: In numerical linear algebra, the conjugate gradient method is an iterative method for numerically solving the linear system A x = b {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {Ax}}={\boldsymbol {b}}} where A {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {A}}} is symmetric positive-definite, without computing A − 1 {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {A}}^{-1}} explicitly.
details: The conjugate gradient method can be derived from several different perspectives, including specialization of the conjugate direction method for optimization, and variation of the Arnoldi/Lanczos iteration for eigenvalue problems. The intent of this article is to document the important steps in these derivations.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Boil it down and it is this: In numerical linear algebra, the conjugate gradient method is an iterative method for numerically solving the linear system A x = b {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {Ax}}={\boldsymbol {b}}} where A {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {A}}} is symmetric positive-definite, without computing A − 1 {\displaystyle {\boldsymbol {A}}^{-1}} explicitly. Here is why it matters: The conjugate gradient method can be derived from several different perspectives, including specialization of the conjugate direction method for optimization, and variation of the Arnoldi/Lanczos iteration for eigenvalue problems. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Derivation of the conjugate gradient method.
